newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Tyumen oil to pay subsidiary tax arrears.
newsitem.headline: Russia Tyumen oil to pay subsidiary tax arrears.

text.p: Russia's Tyumen Oil Company (TNK) will pay off the tax arrears of its main production unit Nizhnevartovskneftegaz by August 25, one of the company's owners said in a statement on Tuesday.

"The State Tax Service of the Russian Federation and OAO Tyumen Oil Company last week signed an agreement by which Tyumen Oil Company will pay ...Nizhnevartovskneftegaz's debt to the budget by August 25 this year," Alfa-Bank said.
The statement did not say how much TNK would pay, but official figures showed Nizhnevartovskneftegaz owed 800 billion roubles ($1.38 million) in back taxes as of July 1, 1997.
Alfa Bank, which won a 40 percent stake in TNK in July, will put up the money, although it is not responsible for company debts under the terms of the auction, the statement said.
A TNK spokesman said previously that Alfa Bank would pay off about $50 million which Ryazan refinery, another TNK subsidiary, owed to the government.

Alfa Bank has said that it wants to win a controlling stake in the company by buying another 48.68 percent stake in the company which was to have been auctioned last week. The sale has been postponed for undisclosed reasons.
TNK is one of six Russian energy companies up for sale in a round of auctions, the starting dates of which were originally set between July 1 and October 21.
TNK is by far the largest of the six and is Russia's fifth or sixth biggest oil company by production. It produced 21.3 million tonnes (426,000 barrels per day) of oil in 1996.
